sourceTitle: Investigating public attitudes to artificial intelligence
author: William Joseph
post: The British public is not simply for or against AI. A nationally representative survey shows where people feel the benefit, and where they want a human in the loop.
alt: Motion graphic of survey findings on public attitudes to AI in Britain, including cancer detection and concern about professional judgement. No photographs of people.

beats.heading: What the public actually thinks about AI
beats.caption: What the public actually thinks about AI.

beats.label: adults in Britain took part in the survey
beats.source: Ada Lovelace Institute and the Alan Turing Institute
beats.caption: More than 4,000 adults in Britain took part in a nationally representative survey.

beats.heading: People are broadly positive.
beats.body: They are also highly specific. The use matters more than the label.
beats.caption: People are broadly positive about AI, and highly specific about each use.

beats.label: find AI for cancer detection broadly beneficial
beats.source: Ada Lovelace Institute and the Alan Turing Institute
beats.caption: 9 in 10 adults find AI for cancer detection broadly beneficial.

beats.label: worry about replacing professional judgement
beats.source: Ada Lovelace Institute and the Alan Turing Institute
beats.caption: 56 percent worry about relying on the technology instead of professional judgement.

beats.heading: People want regulation.
beats.body: That view is not the same in every age group.
beats.caption: People want AI regulation, and that view changes with age.

beats.heading: Design for nuance, not a single opinion.
beats.caption: Design for nuance, not a single public opinion.
